title: Dynamic capacity safety net and graceful fallbacks for noisy tenants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a high-volume weekend surge one tenant generated sustained microbursts that exhausted per-GPU reservation slots and tripped eviction heuristics, causing elevated p95 tail latency for adjacent tenants. The incident combined two factors: an optimistic reservation model that assumed burst smoothing and a burst-credit decay that was too permissive for long, spiky sequences.

Objective: Deliver a lightweight, empirically validated safety-net layer that prevents single-tenant microburst storms from causing eviction cascades while preserving customer-friendly burstability. The solution must include a telemetry-driven autocalibration path, a deterministic graceful fallback to cheaper model variants or reduced batch sizes when safety thresholds are crossed, and an on-call runbook with actionable playbook steps.

Root cause (short): Reservation sizing tuned to median usage rather than sustained 95th percentile; burst-credit leaky-bucket allowed long sequences without decay; no fast-path for graceful degradation to lower-memory model variants; eviction controller reacted too late due to sparse eviction telemetry and lack of tenant soft-fencing metrics.

Impact summary: Several enterprise customers experienced slowed responses (p95 increased 3x) for 18-27 minutes during peak; autoscaler oscillations caused transient pod churn; follow-on support tickets and one urgent escalation from a Dedicated customer.

Outcomes expected: Reduce tenant-induced eviction spikes by 90% in synthetic load tests, ensure degraded-mode latencies remain within SLA bounds for non-impacted tenants, and provide operational visibility + automated mitigation that can be tuned without code changes.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic storm test shows <10% eviction rate compared to baseline when safety-net is enabled
Failover to fallback model maintains p95 for protected tenants within 2x SLA during sustained tenant surge
Autocalibration job computes reservation targets every 6h and surface suggested changes in Console; toggles apply in staging before prod rollout
Runbook steps reproduced end-to-end by SRE runbook drill and documented in Confluence
Dashboards (reservation_usage, burst_credit_balance, tenant_soft_fence) added and firing >90% reliable alerts
work_items: Design safety-net lane: implement soft-fence state machine for tenants and persistent burst-credit with decay coefficient per tenant
Autocalibration job: compute 95th sustained throughput per tenant and propose reservation adjustments in Console
Graceful fallback: add routing policy to switch to a warmed low-memory variant or reduce batch size when soft-fence enters 'throttled' state
Eviction controller hooks: subscribe to tenant soft-fence signal and increase eviction thresholds for adjacent tenants during mitigation window
Telemetry: add tenant_soft_fence, reservation_recommendation, burst_credit_balance metrics and dashboard panels
Runbook: draft playbook for oncall to observe, trigger fallback, and roll back if necessary
E2E tests: synthetic tenant storm harness and chaos test against autoscaler to validate stability
technical_decisions: Use leaky-bucket burst-credit with exponential decay; initial decay tau=900s adjustable via Feature Flag
Fallback model selection prioritized by memory footprint then cost: warmed-quantized -> quantized -> small-architecture
Autocalibration window set to 6h with 24h safety-boundaries; proposals surfaced as Console recommendations rather than automatic applies for first 2 weeks
Soft-fence states: nominal -> watch -> throttled -> penalize. Transition thresholds derived from p95 sustained > reservation * 1.6 for 6m
Implement soft-fence in runtime agent to avoid global coordinator latency; events are eventually-consistent to control blast radius
telemetry_and_alerts: Metric: reservation_usage{tenant} - gauge - alert when >95% for >2min
Metric: burst_credit_balance{tenant} - gauge - alert when drops below configured min
Event: tenant_soft_fence{tenant,state} - event stream used by eviction controller
Grafana dashboard: Dedicated -> Tenant Health -> Soft Fence summary (panel links included in Confluence runbook)
Pager alert: P0 on tenant_eviction_spike with playbook link and escalation path
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable safety-net lane for internal tenants and run synthetic storm tests - duration 3 days
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of dedicated hosts selected by low-impact customers - monitor 48h
Phase 3 (ramp): 50% roll for 24h, evaluate telemetry and customer-facing metrics
Phase 4 (prod): full enablement with autocalibration in recommendation-only mode for 2 weeks, then switch to auto-apply behind opt-in flag after sign-off
security_and_compliance_notes: No customer data movement changes. Fallback models will maintain same data residency and encryption expectations. Any feature-flagged autocalibration suggestions are stored in control-plane only with standard RBAC. Security review not required for initial rollout but will be triggered if fallback involves model variants with different license constraints.
updates: 2026-03-06: Initial triage concluded; assigned to Marcelo. Draft playbook outline created and shared with SRE and runtime teams.
2026-03-07: Prototype leaky-bucket burst-credit implemented in runtime agent; found missing decay edge-case when tenant remains idle for >1hr.
2026-03-08: Telemetry panels sketched; added tenant_soft_fence event to debug stream. SRE requested slower decay during night windows to avoid false positives.
2026-03-10: Integration test shows fallback routing to warmed-quantized model reduced p95 by 60% in synthetic storm; discovered routing lock that delayed fallback by 4s - fixed in PR#4128.
2026-03-12: Draft runbook reviewed with oncall; canary checklist and rollback steps added. Preparing for staging rollout next week.
notes: Trade-offs: conservative autocalibration avoids surprising capacity changes for customers but requires manual acceptance at first. Soft-fence approach prefers targeted tenant throttling over aggressive evictions to reduce blast radius. Future work includes exposing per-tenant reservation suggestions to billing and to customer console for transparency.
